notes: Type PAL visual editor (@type-pal/editor, React), the repo's main phase-2 product surface. Tooling is pinned in mise.toml at the repo root: node 22.23.2 and pnpm 10.29.2, matching CI. Install ran as `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, then esbuild's install.js was run by hand. The optional `canvas` devDependency (only used by phase-1 game tests) needs node-gyp, so it is skipped. Build: `VITE_PROJECT_ID=pal vite build` in packages/editor (output in packages/editor/dist). With VITE_PROJECT_ID baked in, the editor skips the project picker and auto-loads the repo's PAL author project, as the repo's own `pnpm --filter @type-pal/editor dev` does. start.sh first runs .ui-capture/seed-save-state.mjs (idempotent). It writes projects/pal/.type-pal/save-state.json, a gitignored per-workspace file, holding the 'committed' author-save record the editor's own save journal leaves after a completed save (format from packages/reforge/src/project-save-state.ts). An established workspace has this file, and without it the editor's startup probe shows up as a 404. start.sh then runs `vite preview` on $PORT. The editor's vite config adds middleware so preview also serves /projects/* from <repo>/projects (project JSON, maps, RLE assets, editor libraries) and /soundfont.sf3 for music preview. No backend, accounts or external services: everything is local files, so no stubs. Data is the repo's committed, fully migrated PAL content project (projects/pal, about 144 MB): 294 scenes, 223 maps, 1934 catalog assets, plus actors, items, skills, enemies, enemy teams, battle fields, shops, shared scripts, world variables, locale strings, stamps, a saved battle-simulator library and a script-preview library. This is the state of a long-running authoring project. `check-project` passes on it, and the editor's real HTTP boot path (dev workspace proof, project load, all scenes) was verified against the preview server. Headless Chromium could not run in the sandbox, so no screenshot was taken. Main areas: workspace tabs for scenes/maps (tile brush and layer editing on canvas), entities and NPC scripts, the script editor, characters/actors, items and shops, enemies and battle data with the battle simulator, assets, project settings, reference diagnostics, undo/redo and in-editor play preview (/play.html). /design-lab.html is the design-system lab. Saving to disk needs File System Access authorization and is not required for viewing.
